lesson_title: Two Owners, Separate Scorecards: Partnership Capital, Current Accounts and Adjustments
hook_text: Two friends. One till. Whose money is whose?
clip_script: Two friends open a kota shop. Thabo puts in R40 000, Sipho puts in R30 000. Write those numbers on the wall and never touch them — that is capital, money planted like a tree. It moves only if someone formally plants more or digs some out. But every week things flow: Sipho works the counter, so he earns a bigger salary. Thabo planted more, so he earns more interest. Sipho takes airtime and bread — drawings. You cannot scribble all that over the wall, so each friend gets a scorecard: the current account. Earnings on one side, takings on the other. Scorecard in credit — the shop owes the friend. Scorecard in debit — the friend has eaten ahead of his earnings. That is a partnership: the wall shows what was planted, the scorecard shows what is owed, and a written agreement decides the salaries, the interest and the split. Then at year end, honesty edits before the photo: the phone bill that hasn't arrived still counts, the rent paid early doesn't count yet, and five percent of the debtors get dimmed — because someone always fails to pay, you just don't know who yet.
visual_style: A kota shop wall with two painted capital figures that never move, while animated scorecards fill and empty beside them; warm township-shopfront palette, chalkboard textures, coins flowing along drawn arrows.
pacing: Steady build from wall to scorecards, then a quick-fire montage of the honesty edits.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort every amount yourself — planted or flowing.
